rationale: Across reported cohorts with autosomal dominant distal hereditary motor neuropathy 11 (dHMN11, OMIM #620528) harboring heterozygous loss-of-function/nonsense variants in SPTAN1, individuals present with juvenile- or adult-onset distal motor neuropathy (weakness, atrophy, foot deformities, hypo/areflexia) without central nervous system involvement. Severe intractable epilepsy (HP:0001250) and intellectual disability or global developmental delay (HP:0001249/HP:0001263) characterize distinct allelic disorders, notably developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 5 (DEE5/EIEE5, OMIM #613477), which are primarily caused by dominant-negative in-frame or specific missense alterations rather than the haploinsufficiency/nonsense alleles causing pure dHMN11.

evidence.text: dHMN11 is caused by heterozygous nonsense/loss-of-function variants in SPTAN1 and leads to juvenile- or adult-onset distal hereditary motor neuropathy, while complex neurodevelopmental phenotypes, severe intellectual disability, and early-onset epileptic encephalopathy with brain atrophy represent distinct SPTAN1-associated syndromes.
